page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is a virtual server belonging to the High Performance server family. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor configured with 4 vCPUs, which are mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz under a shared allocation model. System memory capacity is 8.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 180 GB NVMe SSD. The server also includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test yielded an average score of 1450.08, whereas the multi-core score of 5759.17 falls into the lower performance tier. Similarly, Geekbench scores show weak single-core (1059.0) and multi-core (3411.0) results. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for cached small-block reads at 416.34 GB/sec and large-block writes at 27.94 GB/sec, but uncached large-block reads are weaker at 33.43 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform well, averaging 6.06 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is lower at 4.88 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a cost-effective option for workloads that require NVMe storage and multi-vCPU configurations without requiring dedicated CPU execution. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential performance variability, which is reflected in the weaker multi-threaded benchmark results, such as the bzip3 multi-threaded decompression score of 17.62 GB/sec. This hardware profile is suitable for lightweight web serving, basic Redis caching, text processing, and development environments that do not demand sustained, high-intensity multi-core processing.

Benchmark data reveals average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1450.08, but weaker multi-core scaling, as seen in its Geekbench multi-core score of 3411.0. The shared CPU allocation presents a tradeoff between cost efficiency and performance stability. This server is best suited for lightweight database operations, Redis caching, basic text processing, and general-purpose development workloads that benefit from fast local NVMe storage but do not require dedicated CPU resources.
